scenes.vo: In January twenty twenty-four, Hertz said it would sell about twenty thousand of its electric cars.
About a third of its global electric fleet. The expected hit: about two hundred forty-five million dollars.

visual.note: ≈20,000 EVs · about one-third of Hertz's global EV fleet

scenes.vo: In twenty twenty-one, Hertz had announced plans to buy one hundred thousand Teslas. So why sell?
Because a rental car's real cost is the price paid, minus what it sells for later.

visual.headline:
THE REAL COST
OF A RENTAL CAR

items.text: = the real cost of owning it

scenes.vo: In twenty twenty-three, new electric car prices fell, led by Tesla. Hertz's CEO said that dragged down the value of its electric cars.

visual.quote: MSRP declines in EVs over the course of 2023, driven primarily by Tesla, have driven the fair market value of our EVs *lower*…
visual.who: Stephen Scherr, Hertz CEO · Q3 2023 earnings call, Oct 2023

scenes.vo: Hertz also said collision and damage costs, mostly on its electric cars, stayed high.

visual.headline:
TWO COSTS,
SAME CARS
visual.source: Source: Hertz statement, Jan 2024 (Axios) · Hertz Form 8-K, 11 Jan 2024

scenes.vo: When you own the asset, someone else's price cut becomes your loss.

visual.display: When you own the asset, someone else's price cut becomes *your* *loss.*
